scope: Independent published Drosophila physiology used to constrain model calibration. These data are not MaleCNS v1.0 body-ID-resolved physiology and remain cross-dataset priors.

sources.title: A neural circuit for wind-guided olfactory navigation
evidence: Wind-sensitive PFN pathways carry directional wind information while odor-sensitive fan-shaped-body tangential pathways carry odor context.
hDeltaC neurons receive both pathways and exhibit odor-gated, wind-direction-tuned activity.
hDeltaC activity is required for persistent upwind orientation during odor in the reported preparation.

sources.title: Converting an allocentric goal into an egocentric steering signal
evidence: FC2 activity correlates with goal angle and EPG activity represents heading.
Individual PFL3 cells show conjunctive spike-rate tuning to heading and goal angle during goal-directed navigation.
Quantitative analysis and optogenetic manipulation support an egocentric steering computation in PFL3 output.

sources.title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
evidence: Targeted in vivo electrophysiology shows DNa02 firing predicts high-gain steering.
Dual recordings show rotational velocity is approximately linearly related to right-left DNa02 firing-rate difference across the measured dynamic range.
A 150 ms neural-to-behavior comparison lag was used, but the authors explicitly note that this lag may reflect biological delay and/or spherical-treadmill inertia.

claim_boundary: These publications provide independent measured physiological constraints and causal/behavioral evidence in other Drosophila preparations. They do not measure activity of the exact MaleCNS v1.0 body IDs and therefore cannot be promoted to MaleCNS-specific measured physiology.
